title: Sensation and perception compared

draft.title: Sensation and perception compared
card: the detecting of stimuli from the body or the world by sense receptors. A stimulus is anything that can be detected, such as light or sound.
the brain selecting, organising and interpreting sensory information so that it has meaning.
Sensation comes first and supplies the raw information. Perception turns it into something we recognise, such as a friend's face or a familiar song.
Two people can receive the same sensory information and perceive it differently, because perception involves interpretation.
draft.remember: Sensation detects the stimulus. Perception gives it meaning.

a.q: Which of these is an example of perception rather than sensation?
opts: Recognising a sound as your phone's ringtone
Light landing on receptors at the back of the eye
Receptors in the ear detecting a sound wave
Skin receptors detecting pressure from a touch
a.why: Recognising a sound as a ringtone means the brain has interpreted the information and given it meaning. The other options describe receptors detecting a stimulus, which is sensation.
a.clue: Which one involves the brain giving meaning to the input?

b.q: Priya hears a noise in the hallway at night and decides it is her cat, not a burglar. Which part of her response is perception?
opts: Deciding the noise is her cat
Her ears detecting the sound wave
Sound reaching receptors in her ears
Her ears picking up the noise at all
b.why: Deciding the noise is her cat is the brain interpreting the information, so it is perception. Detecting the sound is sensation, even though it led to the interpretation.
b.clue: Which part is about what the noise means?

a.best: Recognising a sound as your phone's ringtone

b.best: Deciding the noise is her cat
